Implementation Plan

PLAN — Issue: re-triage PR #6611's CI "shard 1" failure (re-issued from #6932)

Planning ref
- `git rev-parse HEAD` at planning: `4fca6c5ddd5dc9e2f9daff6352791d282256c203`, branch `main`. The planning context recorded `f25804118f7e…` because `main` moved on in between.
- No integration branch is declared, so there is no mismatch. PR #6611 is merged into `main`, so per AD-1 / Q1=A any fix PR targets `main`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends .github/workflows/ci.yml `orchestrate-poll` job ("Derive orchestrate poll test subsets" + "Orchestrate poll process unit tests" step bodies)
Scope-mode justification: The issue is a diagnose-then-act task, and the approved answers fix its scope. Q1=A: a fix goes to `main` because #6611 is merged. Q2=A: shard 1 is rebuilt locally with the CI step's own partition logic. Q3=A: if nothing reproduces, the only deliverable is a findings note. Nothing here widens scope into workflow or sharding changes, and nothing shrinks it below the approved answers. The reproduction reuses the existing CI step bodies verbatim rather than a new harness, so it runs exactly the test set CI ran. Under the §6 priorities (Correctness > Speed), the complete option is to run every group's shard 1 and not guess which group failed. It costs only runtime and no code, so it is chosen.

1. Files likely to change
- NEW `docs/triage/pr-6611-ci-shard-1.md`. This is the default deliverable and the only file changed when nothing reproduces (Q3=A). `docs/triage/` does not exist yet; create it.
- Conditional, only if a failure reproduces deterministically on the current `main` tip: the single file the failing assertion or process error implicates. That is either `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` (if the test itself is wrong, decided from documented behaviour per the heal-prompt rule, not "match the code") or the script under test, typically `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. Fix the root cause with the minimum change, and write the same triage note recording the cause.
- No edits to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`, the `lint` aggregate, the fast-fail selection, or any sandbox/isolation helper.

2. Functions / modules to implement
None new. The reproduction procedure is:
  a. Resolve the target SHAs.
     - Try `git cat-file -t bef70791b7c6` (the failing PR head). At planning time it is not resolvable: the checkout has one commit of history and the squash-merged `ai/issue-6607` head is absent. The sandbox has no network, so do not try to fetch it.
     - Record "failing head unavailable; reproduced at main tip `<sha>`" in the note.
  b. Rebuild the inputs. Run the "Derive orchestrate poll test subsets" Python body from ci.yml (lines ~1551-1582) verbatim. It writes `/tmp/orchestrate_poll_fast_fail_tests.txt` and `/tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt`.
  c. Run the fast-fail subset once, as matrix group 0 does: `python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <fast-fail names>`.
  d. Run the "Orchestrate poll process unit tests" `run:` body (ci.yml ~1597-1730) for each of the four groups. Use `CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_INDEX=0..3`, `CI_POLL_TEST_GROUP_COUNT=4`, `CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS=4`, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. Keep all four local shards running concurrently: timing and CPU contention are part of the CI environment, and a timing-sensitive failure may only appear under concurrency.
     - Assumption, recorded in the note: "shard 1" means local shard 1 of the failed `orchestrate-poll (g)` job. Which group failed is unknown because the job log is auth-walled. So every group's shard 1 is examined, and the other shards are run too. This covers both readings: "matrix group 1" and "local shard 1".
     - Save each `/tmp/poll_shard_1.log` per group before the next group's `rm -f` wipes it.
  e. Read the result.
     - From each failed shard log, capture the first `  FAIL  <name>:` line, or the first traceback/process error if there are no FAIL lines.
     - Re-run each failing test alone (`python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <name>`), 3 times.
     - If it fails only under the concurrent run, re-run just that shard's list 3 times. This separates a deterministic failure from a flaky one.
  f. Decide.
     - A deterministic failure on `main`: apply the smallest root-cause fix, re-run the single test plus that group's full shard set, and record before/after in the note.
     - A failure that is flaky only: record the frequency and conditions in the note, with no code change. The spec forbids speculative fixes.
     - No failure: write the note only.
  g. Run `python3 tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py` to confirm the partition contract is untouched.

3. Data structures affected
None. The note is free-form markdown with fixed sections:
- `## Target`: PR #6611, failing run 37922279826, job 113792812346, failing head `bef70791b7c6` and whether it resolved, and the main tip SHA tested.
- `## Assumptions`: what "shard 1" was taken to mean.
- `## Commands`: exact env values and command lines.
- `## Results`: per group/shard test counts, pass/fail, and the first failure if any.
- `## Conclusion`: one of not reproducible / flaky (rate) / reproduced and fixed (cause + fix) / reproduced only at the old head.
- `## CI confirmation`: the statement that the fix PR's own CI `lint` aggregate is the required rerun. Write "pending this PR's CI" here, never "passed".

4. API / interface changes
None. No env vars, flags, labels, log prefixes or workflow inputs are added or renamed.

## Decisions
### D1 — Target ref for reproduction and fix
- Chosen: reproduce and fix on the current `main` tip. Record that `bef70791b7c6` is unresolvable in the sandbox.
- Alternatives considered: fetching the old PR head (no network in the sandbox); pushing to `ai/issue-6607` (merged, so a push there feeds nothing; Q1 rules it out).
- Why: #6611's code now lives on `main` (Q1=A fallback), and only a failure that is still present on `main` justifies a code change.

### D2 — How to identify "shard 1"
- Chosen: run all four matrix groups with 4 concurrent local shards each, using the CI step bodies verbatim, and inspect shard 1 of every group.
- Alternatives considered: running only group 1; running the whole module sequentially.
- Why: the job id does not reveal the group without the auth-walled log. Running the exact partition under concurrency is the faithful reproduction, and the cost is only about 20 minutes of runtime.

### D3 — Deliverable when nothing reproduces
- Chosen: commit only `docs/triage/pr-6611-ci-shard-1.md`.
- Alternatives considered: no commit (no-op re-issue loop); `BLOCKED:` (the predecessor's dead end).
- Why: Q3=A. It gives a durable record with no speculative code or workflow change.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none are crossed. The work is local test execution in the credential-free implement sandbox. The note must not include tokens, env dumps, or remote URLs. Copy test names and assertion text only, after a quick check for credential-like strings.
- Authorization: no new endpoint, workflow, or surface.
- External input: shard logs are local output. Quote them in fenced code blocks in the note so no line can be read as markdown or as a routing marker. Strip any `<!-- ai:` sequences from quoted log lines.
- Abuse cases:
  - Weakening the `lint` aggregate, the shard-failure tally (`.rc`-missing ⇒ failure), the fast-fail step, or sandbox isolation to make CI green. This is forbidden; a reviewer should reject any diff touching `ci.yml` or the sharding tests.
  - Rewriting a test assertion to match current code without documented-behaviour evidence. Also forbidden.

Data flow:
1. Derive subsets (ci.yml Python body), which writes the fast-fail and remaining lists.
2. Fast-fail run (once).
3. For g in 0..3: group slice (`NR%4==g`), then 4 concurrent shards (`NR%4==s`), then save the per-shard logs.
4. Triage the first failures, re-run them in isolation, and classify them (deterministic, flaky or none).
5. Then either a fix plus re-run, or no fix. Write the note, and run the sharding contract test.

Failure modes:
- Old head unresolvable. Symptom: `git cat-file` fails. Recovery: test `main`, and record it in the note. This is expected.
- A group's shard logs are overwritten by the next group's `rm -f`. Recovery: copy `/tmp/poll_shard_*.log` into a per-group directory after each run.
- The step body references `strategy.job-index` etc. via `env:` only. Recovery: export the three env vars by hand. The body itself has no `${{ }}`, apart from the `env:` block, which is replaced by exports.
- The fix touches `scripts/` (an automation path). Symptom: `IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD` rejects the commit unless the issue grants that exact path in `files_touched`. Recovery: keep the fix out of the commit. Record the demonstrated cause, the exact one-line fix and the failing test in the note, so a follow-up can carry the grant. Do not try to bypass the guard.
- A cold local runner is slower than CI and the run times out. Recovery: run groups one by one, and note the wall time.

5. Risks and edge cases
- Conflict: the spec says "on the PR branch". #6611 is merged (GITHUB FACTS, AD-1), so this plan targets `main` as Q1=A's fallback requires.
- Conflict: the failing head `bef70791b7c6` cannot be resolved in this checkout (single-commit history). A failure that existed only at the old head cannot be reproduced. In that case the note concludes "not reproducible on main; old head unavailable".
- A flaky failure may need many repetitions. Cap it at 3 isolated and 3 shard-level re-runs, and record the rate instead of fixing.
- The sandbox has a different CPU count from `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU). Record `nproc` in the note.
- Changelog: CLAUDE.md §20 decides whether a fragment is needed. A docs-only triage note is not user-visible behaviour, so add no fragment unless a code fix lands. In that case add `changelog.d/<issue>-pr-6611-shard-1-fix.
